findings.detail: The updated docs and changelog say GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B are declared for public cluster traffic in pipeline and tensor parallel. A coordinator derives their qualifications from a checked-in declaration (`ClusterPublicModels`) and applies them to the whole declared family "on any Apple silicon pair", because "the placement names the evidence, not a limit". The changelog admits that no pipeline ran on two M5 Ultras and that GLM-5.3-Flash has no tensor-parallel cross-cable record, so both rest on the owner's decision. Pair members report only hardware capabilities, so a grant is the only gate on who may serve consumer prompts. A provider (ADV-001) with a different chip or memory class could then serve public traffic under a qualification never exercised on that hardware or mode. That risks wrong outputs or an incorrectly trusted build, which T-054 and T-056 treat as limits of attestation. The threat model does not describe this declaration-derived qualification path or the new `cluster_runtime` release registration. It should record that parity evidence does not cover the applied scope, and name who may change the declaration.
findings.title: Public cluster qualification extended to any Apple silicon pair on owner decision, beyond evidence placement

findings.detail: The new text says a signed release posts `cluster_runtime` to `POST /v1/releases`, and the coordinator derives cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications from it. Qualifications for GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B are declared by the build (`ClusterPublicModels`). Their evidence is an owner decision plus a document hash, not cross-cable records, and the docs say no M5 Ultra pipeline run and no GLM TP record exists. The coordinator applies a promotable record to the whole mode family on any numerics classes, cuts and shares, so public traffic is admitted on any Apple silicon pair. Whoever can call the release API (A-005), or whoever controls a release's declaration, can now create public-serving qualification as well as binary trust. That weakens the independent-qualification assumption behind A-017, T-052 and T-054, and the threat model has no entry for this derivation path. The control is outside the supplied evidence, so the coordinator-side authorization of `cluster_runtime` is unverified. Fix: update A-005, A-017 and T-054 to cover release-derived qualifications, and confirm the coordinator requires independent approval of the `cluster_runtime` block rather than trusting the release key alone.
findings.title: Release-registered cluster_runtime now mints public-traffic approvals, grants and parity qualifications; threat model does not cover it
